These conduits grow from one root, marked with the same pips. Turning either one turns them all, however far apart they sit.
Thorns have grown across two of this tile's four ways. Light passes along the other two, and turning the tile swings the thorns round onto them - so a bramble never opens a way without shutting one.

The colour in your hand MIXES into whatever flower you tap - red with yellow in hand turns orange.

Get three of one colour touching and they burst, splashing that colour into every flower around them. Which makes more threes. Which makes more.

A critter is shut in until a burst goes off right beside it.

You cannot tap a cocoon open - you have to set something off next to it. The ones drawn with a second ring take two.

This grove is dealt so many taps and no more.

There is no undo, and nothing grows back - so the fewer taps you free everyone in, the more stars you keep.

Two flows pass through this tile and never meet. It wears no hub, and that is how you tell it from a junction: follow each strand with your eye, because light that enters by one arm can only leave by the arm that shares its strand.
This one sleeps in the shade, and wears a moon to say so. Any light at all wakes it, and the glade will not settle until every duskcap is dark again.
This one crumbles after a few turns — the number shows how many are left. Undoing does not mend it.

A mote adds its colour to the one it lands on. Red on yellow makes orange.

A mote holding all three bursts, and washes that colour into everything beside it.

This well is dealt so many motes and no more.

There is no undo here. Watch the ring under your thumb before you let go.

A mote that comes to rest above the line ends the run.

A colour the top of a stack already holds is what raises it - the ring turns red when it would.

A lens fills one colour at a time - free from any burst beside it, or a drop at a time by hand.

Fill all three and it fires white to left and right, popping whatever each beam lands on.

Light one lens with another and it fires every way - up and down as well.

This is the corner of the groove that is yours. Every friend you rescue and every piece you buy can stand here, wherever you decide. Tap a tile to put something on it, and hold what you have placed to move or turn it.
Everything a groove is made of is in here: friends to live in it, decor to fill it and more ground to build on. Credits come from clearing glades, and nothing you buy is ever used up.

This button spins a wheel of fortune for extra coins on top of what the glade paid. Spinning costs nothing and every slice is equally likely - the best one is worth five times the rest. It is here after every glade you earn coins on.
This critter dreams of a colour no single heart carries. Join two hearts into one network and their light blends — red and yellow make orange.
There is more than one way to play. Tap here to swap between them — each has its own map and its own levels, and every one is open to you from the very first day.
This is how many turns you have left. Run out with the glade still dark and it costs a heart.
A rooted tile cannot be turned. Treat it as a fixed part of the path and route the rest of the groove around it.

A tile goes beside the groove, never on its own.

One that gathers all three colours - counting its neighbours - bursts into bloom. Two of a colour together are worth nothing.

This groove is dealt so many tiles and no more, in the order the basket shows.

There is no undo here. The ring under your thumb says what a tile would open before you let go.

Nothing may be planted on stone, and no light passes through it.

A bed beside one has fewer neighbours to gather from, so what it is missing has to come from a shorter list of cells.

The key beside the basket spends the tile in your hand without planting it, and brings the next one round.

It costs a tile like any other. Sometimes that is the cheapest move there is.

A bed drawn in a colour takes that colour and no other. Anything else is refused outright, so nothing can be spoiled by a stray tap.

Count forward through the basket, and compost what is in the way.

A prism carries all three colours at once. It blooms wherever it lands and opens any bed, heartbed included.

There is only one. Spend it where two ordinary tiles could not.

The groove's route is how many turns this glade was built around. Winning only needs every lamp lit, so conduits you never touch can stay as they are — which is how a run can come in shorter.
